title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E410 (1771) sets up the equilibrium of a plane line-body that is either perfectly flexible or elastic. At a cut at M, the action of the part AM on M is replaced by two forces. T is the force along the tangent MT. V is a force normal to the curve, acting along the line vp at lever arm Mv = v. At the neighbouring point m (with Mm = ds) these become T+dT, V+dV and v+dv. The element Mm carries external loads p ds along the tangent and q ds along the normal.

This page does the force bookkeeping.
(1) Let dΦ be the angle between the tangents MT and mt, so dΦ = ds/r with r the radius of curvature.
(2) Resolve T+dT, which acts along mt, into:
  - the component along mT (parallel to MT): (T+dT)cos dΦ ≈ T+dT;
  - the component along mR (normal): (T+dT)sin dΦ ≈ T dΦ + dT dΦ.
(3) Slide the normal force V+dV along its line of action to the point u where it meets the line mT. To first order mu = mv = v+dv. Resolve it into:
  - the component along uT: (V+dV)dΦ;
  - the component along the normal us: V+dV.
(4) Equilibrium of the element requires these four components to be equivalent to T along MT, V along VP, and the element loads p ds and q ds.

The next page turns this into three equations:
- tangential force balance: dT + V dΦ = p ds;
- normal force balance: dV − T dΦ = q ds;
- moment balance: d(Vv) = V ds, i.e. bending moment M = Vv with dM/ds = V.

In modern form these are the planar Kirchhoff–Clebsch rod equations with shear force, written in intrinsic (Frenet) components.
errors: Not an error but loose: the second-order term dT·dΦ is kept in component II and then dropped later. The approximations cos dΦ ≈ 1 and mu = mv (strictly mu = mv/cos dΦ) are correct only to first order. This is consistent with the infinitesimal method.
The sign conventions for the normal components are left implicit and are only fixed on the next page through 'quatenus in eandem partem tendunt'. Correct, but under-specified on this page.

ideas.what: Cut principle: the action of one part of the body on the other at a section is replaced by a tangential force T, a normal (shear) force V and a lever arm v (equivalently a couple Vv).
ideas.modern_name: Stress resultants (tension, shear force, bending moment) of a rod; Euler's cut principle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, E410 (1771), as emphasized by Truesdell (1960); earlier partial forms in James Bernoulli and Euler 1744
ideas.where_published: E410 itself; analysed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies 1638–1788 (Opera omnia II 11/2)

ideas.what: Resolution of the forces at the neighbouring section into intrinsic tangent/normal components using the contingence angle dΦ = ds/r.
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic (Frenet) balance of linear momentum for a curved rod
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (also used for strings by Johann Bernoulli and Euler earlier)
ideas.where_published: E410; similar resolutions in Euler's earlier string and elastica papers

ideas.what: Prepared balance laws dT + V dΦ = p ds, dV − T dΦ = q ds, d(Vv) = V ds (derived on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Planar rod equilibrium equations n' + f = 0, m' + t×n = 0 (Kirchhoff/Clebsch/Love form)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler 1771 (E410) per Truesdell; later generalized by Kirchhoff and Clebsch

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known derivation in E410 that Truesdell singled out as the first general statement of force and moment balance for flexible and elastic lines. The page is a careful but standard component resolution, with nothing beyond what the historical literature already credits to Euler.
transcription_corrections: Line 'resoluta secundum directiones mT et MR': the image reads 'MR' with a capital M, while the later items use 'mR'. This is a minor inconsistency in the original, not a transcription error.
'sec. VP = V' in XI: the image shows 'VP' (capital), matching the original. It refers to the line vp of force V at M.
